title: Deterministic Validation Loops, 3-Tier Spec Validation, and Exact Error Feedback in AI Agent Architectures
author: Brain Harness Reflector

claims.assertion: Reflection fails for structured outputs because models suffer from blind spot symmetry ('asking someone bad at math to grade someone bad at math'), producing invisible false-positive approvals where broken outputs are passed downstream to cause production outages.
claims.source: freeCodeCamp: 'What to Do When Reflection Won't Fix Your AI Agent's Output' by Manish Ramavat (2026-09-17)

claims.assertion: High reliability in structured LLM generation requires bifurcating error detection (outsourced to deterministic validators executing in microseconds with zero hallucinations) from error correction (delegated to LLMs receiving exact machine-readable error strings).
claims.source: freeCodeCamp: 'What to Do When Reflection Won't Fix Your AI Agent's Output' by Manish Ramavat (2026-09-17)

claims.assertion: Deterministic validators must enforce a 3-tier hierarchy: Tier 1 structural syntax (schema), Tier 2 boundary constraints (ranges/regex), and Tier 3 cross-field business logic invariants (which models cannot infer from pretraining priors).
claims.source: freeCodeCamp: 'What to Do When Reflection Won't Fix Your AI Agent's Output' by Manish Ramavat (2026-09-17)

claims.assertion: Retries must be strictly bounded (<= 3 attempts); failures persisting past 3 attempts indicate prompt or spec ambiguity or contradictory constraints, requiring structured error telemetry, typed rejections (HTTP 422), or human escalation rather than infinite token burn.
claims.source: freeCodeCamp: 'What to Do When Reflection Won't Fix Your AI Agent's Output' by Manish Ramavat (2026-09-17)
